name: Himeji-jo
scaleNote: 1 stud per metre. The keep is 46.4 m above its base; six storeys have to be six readable bands.

keepHeight.source: Wikipedia, Himeji Castle: main keep height above base '46.4 m (152 ft)'.

basementArea.source: Wikipedia, Himeji Castle: 'The basement of the main keep has an area of 385 m2 (4,140 ft2)' -- a 19.6 m square, which is where the keep's footprint here comes from.

note: SIX FLOORS AND A BASEMENT, appearing as five from outside -- Wikipedia says so, and the model builds the six. The footprint is the square root of the cited basement area, which is arithmetic on a source rather than a measurement of the building: the keep tapers, so 19.6 m is its widest and the upper storeys step in. The roofs are stepped courses and not eaves; a Japanese roof is a curve this kit cannot cut.
